unit.why: A teaching on Passover stringencies, told by a grandson of R. Avraham 'the Angel', containing a brief anecdote: R. Zusya covered himself in a wheel in winter, was overcome by the awe of the angels and asked God to remove it. The anecdote is wrapped in an extended homiletic frame.
unit.boundary_note: Opens section ח (Passover stringencies); the next division begins a separate story from Sefer Zikhron Tov on the same theme.

stories.start_quote: פ״א היה מדבר מן החומרא של פסח
stories.summary_en: A rebbe discusses Passover stringencies: his grandfather R. Avraham was so strict that the Maggid took him along for baking the commandment matzah, and only an angel could live on his kind of eating. He tells how R. Zusya covered himself in a wheel in winter, was seized by the awe of the angels and asked God to remove it, and then explains this homiletically through Ezekiel's 'ofan'.

tags.why: The anecdote serves a long homily on Ezekiel 1 and Psalm 113.
